sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il VIX a 18,7 (+6,9%) indica una leggera tensione, ma ancora sotto la soglia di panico; il S&P 500 è sceso del 0,35% a 7.592,40, segnale di pressione ribassista. Il DXY è a 103,20 (+0,03%), segno di un dollaro forte che penalizza gli asset rischiosi. L'aumento del Brent a $96,33 (+0,53%) è contenuto da timori di escalation Iran-USA, contribuendo a un contesto geopolitico bearish (+2 punti). La combinazione di VIX medio‑alto, equity in ribasso e dollaro forte porta a un sentiment risk‑off con score 8/10.
sentiment.reason_en: The VIX at 18.7 (+6.9%) shows modest tension but stays below panic levels; the S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40, indicating bearish pressure. The DXY at 103.20 (+0.03%) reflects a strong dollar that drags risk assets. Brent’s rise to $96.33 (+0.53%) is muted by Iran‑US escalation fears, adding a geopolitical bearish factor (+2 points). The mix of a mid‑high VIX, falling equities and a strong dollar yields a risk‑off sentiment with a score of 8 out of 10.

market_impact_summary.it: Alla chiusura, il S&P 500 è -0,35% mentre il VIX è +6,9% a 18,7, segnale di cautela. Il DXY a 103,20 (+0,03%) rende più costoso il capitale per le emergenti; il Brent a $96,33 (+0,53%) resta sotto pressione per le tensioni Iran‑USA. Il TLT è -1,48% a 79,72, confermando la compressione dei rendimenti obbligazionari. Gold guadagna +0,40% a $3.900,70, ma il suo rialzo è mitigato da tassi reali ancora alti, generando un impatto misto.
market_impact_summary.en: At the close, the S&P 500 is down 0.35% while the VIX rose 6.9% to 18.7, indicating caution. The DXY at 103.20 (+0.03%) makes risk capital pricier for emerging markets; Brent sits at $96.33 (+0.53%) but is weighed down by Iran‑US tensions. TLT fell 1.48% to 79.72, confirming bond‑yield compression. Gold rose 0.40% to $3,900.70, yet its gain is tempered by still‑high real rates, yielding a mixed impact.

articles.snippet: Since 2022, Chinese General Secretary Xi Jinping has purged at least 100 senior military officials, according to a February report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies, with more cases occurring since then. The rate of dismissals and disappearances has increased substantially in the last two years. Recent examples include Gen. Zhang Youxia, Gen. Liu Zhenli, and Zhong Shaojun, formerly the head of the General Office of the Central Military Commission. articles.title: The Promise of Biomanufacturing at the Edge
articles.snippet: As the old adage goes, “Amateurs talk strategy. Professionals talk logistics.” Military operations are utterly dependent on complex supply chains to move food, fuel, and other essential products across long distances and through contested environments to reach the warfighter. These vital supply lines are fragile at every stage: production concentrated in a single facility can be disrupted, key inputs may come from unreliable — or adversarial — foreign suppliers, and the ports, airfields, and roads that deliver goods the final mile are often the most vulnerable.The threat of this fragility eroding a modern force’s capabilities is very real. As the The post The Promise of Biomanufacturing at the Edge appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
articles.snippet: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.
